title: LangChain-Parsl: Connect Large Language Model Agents to High Performance Computing Resource
problem: LLM agents can use external tools but lack integration with HPC schedulers and job management systems. Scientific applications require running large simulations on HPCs, which need job scheduler coordination.
motivation: Enable LLM agents to directly invoke HPC-managed tools like molecular dynamics simulations, bridging the gap between LLM tool-calling and distributed HPC resource management.
method: Implement Parsl integration into LangChain tool calling. Two implementations: (1) Modify LangChain tool calls to convert to Parsl functions queued to Parsl workers for parallel execution, (2) Design Parsl ensemble function as LLM tool. Tested on local Nvidia GPU workstation and Polaris/ALCF HPC system with molecular dynamics simulations.
key_novelty: First integration of LLM agents (LangChain) with HPC job scheduling (Parsl) enabling agent-driven HPC simulation execution.
contributions: LangChain-Parsl integration layer for LLM-HPC coordination
Two implementation approaches for tool-to-HPC mapping
Demonstration of parallel execution of scientific tools from LLM agents
Validation on both local GPU and HPC cluster systems

metrics.primary: Parallel execution of LLM-invoked scientific tools

limitations: Abstract does not provide performance metrics or comparison with baseline approaches. Only tested on MD simulations.
primary_theme: LLM Agent Integration with HPC Job Scheduling
